." Numerous studies have shown that voter fraud in U.S. elections is rare, according to the Brennan Center for Justice at New York University School of Law. In a report titled "The Truth About Voter Fraud," the center cited voter fraud incident rates between 0.00004 percent and 0.0009 percent. An August study by The Washington Post found 31 credible cases of impersonation fraud out of more than 1 billion votes cast in elections from 2000 to 2014. Arizona State University studies in 2012 and 2016 found similarly low rates. "Despite this overwhelming evidence, claims that voter fraud is rampant consistently garner media attention, because perceived threats to electoral integrity—even those with no basis in fact—frighten voters by striking at the core of our democracy," Brennan Center counsel Jennifer Clark wrote in a blog last month. Avianca said that until further notice it’s also rerouting several flights to Europe to avoid Venezuelan air space.  “We’re waiting for them to guarantee the security conditions required to operate,” Avianca spokeswoman Gilma Usuga told The Associated Press.
